items.text: Streaming audio submission is documented as safe to call from a producer thread (audio.h Doxygen of cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_submit_buffer: 'That is what makes this route safe to call from a producer thread while playback runs'; docs/c-api/AUDIO.md says the same), but the route resolves the instance with BorrowDynamicInstance -> GetSoundEffectInstance -> HandleRegistry::Get, which returns CNA_RESULT_THREAD for any thread other than the handle's creation thread. The float variant uses the same path. AUDIO.md's own threading section says every audio call must run on the creation thread, so the documents contradict each other and the implementation follows the stricter rule.
items.evidence: modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiAudio.cpp (cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_submit_buffer, cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_submit_float_buffer_ext, BorrowDynamicInstance, GetSoundEffectInstance); modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiDetail.hpp (HandleRegistry::Get creation-thread check); modules/c-api/include/CNA/C/audio.h; docs/c-api/AUDIO.md; modules/c-api/tests/pure_c/AudioStreamingSmoke.c (no second thread)

items.text: MODULE_SCOPE in generate_coverage_inventory.py does not classify modules/design, modules/diagnostics or modules/inspector, so validate_module_scope raises and the coverage and limitations generators exit 2; CApiCoverageMatrix, CApiLimitations, CApiCoverageScopeModel and CApiReleaseGate fail, and the release gate measures two unmet criteria (its --check reports the limitations-matrix disagreement).

items.text: LIMITATIONS.md states 9,355 declarations but partitions only 8,887 (8,363 + 15 + 509); the 468 planned rows are omitted because read_rows keeps only partial and not-applicable rows. The release-gate note still attributes 654 build-time declarations to CBIND-117 (the plan records 134) and omits CBIND-125 and CBIND-127.

graphics_device.h permits destroying a caller-created device while resources made on it are live ('released with it'); cna_graphics_device_destroy counts no children. The resulting state of those still-registered resource handles, and whether the caller must still destroy them, is unspecified and untested (every pure-C test destroys resources first).

cna_graphics_resource_get_graphics_device answers through BorrowGameGraphicsDevice(resource.parentGame); for a resource on a caller-created device the owner token is that device's handle, not a game, so the lookup fails instead of returning the device.

The C library and its tests are exercised by no CI job or preset. The four run configurations in compatibility_matrix.json (headless, sdlrenderer, software, asan) are only rendered into COMPATIBILITY.md; no tool, preset or workflow configures them. Six of the ten release-gate criteria (real C application, installable, documentation, safety evidence, packaged dependencies, static configuration) are satisfied by file, registration or string presence, and the compatibility criterion by document currency (--check), not by compiling.
items.evidence: tools/c-api/check_release_gate.py (check_* functions); tools/c-api/generate_compatibility_matrix.py (configurations rendered only; --check vs --run); CMakePresets.json; .github/workflows/c-api-*.yml

items.text: docs/c-api/HANDLES.md documents CNA_RESULT_SHUTTING_DOWN for a closing or closed runtime (and a different-runtime handle row); no route in modules/c-api/src returns it (only ErrorCategoryForResult maps it), so a stale handle after shutdown answers CNA_RESULT_INVALID_HANDLE.

Documentation drift inside CNA's C API prose: cnb.h's @file comment says the schemas, document, byte cursors and loader registry 'are not published yet' although the header declares them (272 routes); docs/c-api/FEATURE_MATRIX.md describes 'experimental version 0.1.0', '14 capability flags', 'renderer selection remains compile-time' and 50 renderer identities; the CApiReleaseGate comment in ModuleProbes.cmake says two packaging questions await a decision though both criteria are recorded met; core_ext.h speaks of '46 identities'.
items.evidence: modules/c-api/include/CNA/C/cnb.h (@file); docs/c-api/FEATURE_MATRIX.md (Scope, Graphics discovery, Core extensions rows); cmake/Tests/ModuleProbes.cmake (CApiReleaseGate comment); modules/c-api/include/CNA/C/core_ext.h (cna_graphics_renderer_get_is_available_ext)

items.text: OWNERSHIP.md promises that a typed content-load handle stays valid after its manager's Unload or destruction; by reading this holds (Unload only clears the native cache), but no pure-C test uses a loaded resource after unloading or destroying its manager.
